stage1.impression: It reads as a clean CG hi-fi showroom, not a photograph of a night room. The fir-lined niche with its two lit plinths holds up, but the floor is flat, empty brown, the tub chairs are smooth black blobs with no velvet, and a blown, out-of-focus white Orb and a salmon block of table are cut off in the lower-left corner. The smoked speakers read as clear boxes with glowing white batts, so nothing in the frame carries the product's colour. A magazine would not run this as a specific place: it is a generic listening-room or home-cinema render, with no concrete, beams or steel to say where it is.

blocking_9: The shell (board-formed concrete, Douglas fir beams, blackened steel) and the 200 mm step must be legible in frame, so it reads as a specific bar rather than a generic hi-fi room
The tub chairs must read as velvet at 1:1 (sheen on the rims, nap) instead of matte CG solids; chair region [740,530,1095,800] median at least 18
The foreground must be composed, not accidental: no half-cut, defocused, near-clipped Orb disc filling the bottom-left corner
Both altar speakers lit evenly, each region median at least 45, with no white batt panel near clipping, so the smoked acrylic and its edges read
Pools of light on the floor and the tables of the zone, with the floor holding detail (floor median 22 to 40, not falling to 8)
Visible signs of life in the zone (glass, record, coat), and a little atmosphere in the altar spots' beams
Soffit hotspots in the niche below 0.5 % clipping

defects.what: Foreground oak table and two Orb lamps cut by the frame edge; the near Orb is a defocused white disc (median 203) and the oak reads salmon pink and plastic
Tub chairs nearly crushed (median 8.3, crush 9.5 %) and smooth: no velvet sheen or nap, they read as CG solids
The zone floor is a featureless dark plane (lum range 29, falling from 28 to 9 toward the camera); no concrete, no rug texture, no reflections, no pools of light
The left speaker's upper white batt is nearly clipped (median 242) and flat, so it reads as a white card behind clear plastic; the smoke tint is lost
The right speaker is under-lit compared with the left (median 35.8 against 61.1), so the pair is lopsided
The right horn shows a busy, high-contrast mirror reflection that reads as an environment map rather than resin
Downlight hotspots on the fir soffit clip (1.67 %)
The screen image on the left wall reads as a grey, out-of-focus poster with no glow, an unexplained grey rectangle
The ceiling beam is crushed to near black (median 5.5); no fir grain or checks visible, so the shell does not register
The niche's fir planks are uniform and repeating, with no checks, colour variation or end grain, so they read as a tiled texture

changes.problem: The altar pair is lit unevenly and the left batt nearly clips while the right speaker falls below legibility.

evidence.measured: right speaker median 35.8 (needs 45 or more); left speaker [410,270,520,485] median 61.1; left upper batt [418,342,512,380] median 241.6

change.to: 55 W, cone 20 deg, both re-aimed at the cabinet centre (about 0.75 m above the plinth) from slightly to the side, so the light grazes the acrylic faces rather than hitting the batts head-on

changes.expected: Both cabinets sit at a similar mid-tone (median 50 to 70), the acrylic edges catch a line of light, and the batts stay below about 215.

changes.problem: The zone has no pools of light: the Orbs barely light their tables, so the chairs and floor crush.

evidence.measured: chairs median 8.3, crush 9.5 %; floor [200,520,740,800] median 17.2, falloff 28 to 9 toward the camera

change.to: 1.0 W, glow 0.004 (more light thrown down onto the table and floor, a less blown liner)

changes.expected: A warm pool under each oak table spills onto the chair arms and floor, and the chairs hold shape (median about 18 to 30).

changes.problem: The lower-left corner is an accident: a half-cut table and a defocused near-white Orb disc pull the eye from the altar, and the shell (beams, concrete, step) is out of frame or crushed.

evidence.measured: near Orb [0,700,140,800] median 203; the table oak reads r159 g114 b94 (salmon); beam [0,0,290,140] median 5.5

change.to: position about [12.6, 1.6, 1.15] (seated eye level, further from the table), lens 30 mm, f/5.6, framed so one tub chair and its oak table with its Orb sit whole in the lower-left third, the step edge crosses the lower frame, and a fir beam and a strip of board-formed concrete stay at the top and left edges

changes.expected: The foreground becomes a deliberate, readable vignette (a lamp, a glass, a chair), the altar stays the focal point, and the shell's materials tell the reader where this is.

changes.problem: The velvet tub chairs read as smooth CG solids, with no sheen and no nap.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 37.8 with no rim highlight; at 3x crop the surface is uniform

change.setting: the materials' finish: tub chair velvet
change.to: sheen weight 0.8, sheen roughness 0.35, base roughness 0.9, with a faint nap and crush-mark normal map at about 3 mm scale

changes.expected: Bright velvet rims and edges where the Orb light grazes, a darker body, and a believable fabric.

changes.problem: The zone floor is a featureless dark plane that gives no material and no reflection of the lit niche.

change.setting: the materials' finish: the floor's polish
change.to: lightly polished (roughness about 0.3) with tonal mottling and faint trowel and pour variation, so the niche and the plinth pools reflect softly

changes.expected: A soft, warm reflection of the niche running toward the camera, and visible floor texture.

changes.problem: The fir soffit shows clipped downlight scallops.

change.setting: lamps: the altar spots' source size and the soffit fir finish
change.to: a 40 mm source radius with a recessed baffle, and the fir sheen lowered to oiled matte (roughness 0.6), so the scallop fades rather than burns

changes.expected: Soft scallops under the fixtures, with no clipping on the wood.

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere: the altar's spots and the downlights have no visible beams, so the room feels airless and rendered.

evidence.measured: dark gaps between the speakers and the boards sit near 50 with hard edges, and no veil is visible

changes.expected: Faint cones under the altar spots and a slight lift and softening in the niche's shadows, without greying the blacks.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life in the frame: the props in the zone are out of shot or unreadable.

evidence.measured: seen: no glass, record or coat readable anywhere in the lower half

change.from: a record and sleeve, a sleeve against a plinth and a coat over a tub chair, none readable from this camera
change.to: a rocks glass with a finger of whisky and a record out of its sleeve on the foreground oak table under the Orb; the coat over the arm of the nearest tub chair; a sleeve leaning on the right plinth, its edge catching the altar spot

changes.expected: Small highlights on the glass and the vinyl in the Orb's pool give the room scale and life.

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked tint of the Atmosphere cabinets more visible, so the speaker is read as the coloured hero
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour and parts are fixed by the configuration (Smoke). Lighting (c1) can only help the tint read; a stronger tint would be a product change.

out_of_scope.request: Calm the right horn's busy mirror reflection by changing the horn's resin finish
out_of_scope.why: The horn is part of the fixed product. Only the reflected environment can change, which c3 and c1 address indirectly.

out_of_scope.request: Show more of the board-formed concrete and steel shell inside the niche
out_of_scope.why: The niche's lining (Douglas fir) and the room's layout are fixed. Only the camera (c3) can bring the shell into frame.
